subject: Tenancy model & SLO asks — follow-up from Thursday call
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@medisync.com>, procurement@medisync.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Feb 2027 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Tenancy model & SLO asks — follow-up from Thursday call

Hi Alicia / team,

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation and helpful context on Medisync's latency sensitivity for triage workflows. Quick post-call recap and concrete asks so we can scope a clean pilot: 

Summary of options we discussed:
- Hosted API: fastest to get started; shared infra with soft isolation and configurable rate limits. Good for low-to-medium throughput and tight time-to-value.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool for Medisync; predictable throughput and stronger isolation (no noisy-neighbor exposure).
- Private VPC / on-prem: full network isolation, customer-managed control plane, KMS/HSM integration — recommended for regulated PHI flows.

Key SLO / security items we need to confirm for the pilot:
1) Target latency SLOs (p95 token latency and end-to-end request p95). You mentioned 200–300ms for simple prompts — can you confirm p95 target for peak and off-peak?
2) Expected traffic profile for the POC: peak RPS, average sequence length, and daily token volume.
3) Data residency & encryption requirements (VPC, KMS, retention windows).
4) Any procurement gating items / required contract terms (PO timeline, specific SOC2 evidence).

Attached is a short options brief (RWI-tenancy-options.pdf) and the typical pilot checklist. Proposed next steps:
- You confirm the three items above by EOD Wednesday 2/10
- Redwood will produce a one-page POC plan with recommended mode (we can recommend Dedicated with prefix-KV caching if peak RPS > 200)
- Schedule a technical deep-dive if you want kernel-level/sequence-length benchmarking in the POC

If it helps, I can pull in Vanessa to detail the noisy-neighbor protections and how our routing/fallbacks work.

Thanks,
Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mateo@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Tenancy model & SLO asks — follow-up from Thursday call

Hi Alicia — looping in with the technical clarifications Mateo offered. Short answers up front, then specific asks for the POC sizing.

1) Hosted API exposure: primarily tail latency variability. We rely on continuous batching and shared pools; individual tenant throttles are request-rate based (we enforce per-tenant RPS quotas) rather than token-level throttles. In practice: a noisy tenant can increase p99 for others if they generate extremely long sequences at peak, but p95 and p50 are generally stable for well-behaved workloads.

2) Dedicated capacity: no shared scheduling with other tenants — dedicated GPU pool, reserved kernels. Lead time for a standard POC reservation is typically 10 business days once a PO/commit is in place; we can often do expedited reservations for short pilots if capacity exists.

3) Private VPC / on-prem: full network isolation, supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and air-gapped deployments. Requires longer procurement and infra setup (3–6 weeks typical).

SLA / SLO mechanics we propose for the POC:
- Observable metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (token and end-to-end), successful completion rate, model quality regressions (basic eval set we agree on).
- Fallbacks & graceful degradation: automatic fallback to smaller model family or to cached responses for known prefixes. We can surface per-route cost/latency and set auto-fallback thresholds.

POC sizing asks (please provide these so we can finalize the plan):
- Peak concurrent requests (RPS) and expected average sequence length (tokens) per request
- Estimated hourly distribution (peak hours and off-peak) for two weeks
- Data retention needs and whether PHI will transit the host (impacts whether Private VPC is required)

Attached is a short SLA matrix that maps tenancy modes to expected isolation characteristics and lead times. If you confirm the POC numbers above, we will:
- Propose a recommended mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) with a tentative cost estimate
- Draft a two-week POC plan: acceptance criteria, traffic patterns, quality checks, and rollback/fallback triggers

Happy to jump on a quick 30-min tech sync later this week if you prefer — Mateo and I are available Thursday morning.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Attachments: tenancy-sla-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Thanks Vanessa — that's clear and helpful. For the POC we can provide the numbers you requested: 
- Peak concurrent requests: 220 RPS (short 5–10 minute spikes up to 300)
- Average sequence length: 120 tokens (some triage prompts up to 600 tokens occasionally)
- Hourly distribution: US Pacific peak 09:00–15:00 local, off-peak nights
- Data residency: PHI will be present in payloads for the POC — we will need KMS and a VPC option for production; for the POC we can sanitize or pseudo-anonymize if needed.

Procurement: procurement@medisync.com will prepare a PO; we aim to confirm by 3/01 and would prefer a Dedicated pilot if lead time fits. Please propose a Dedicated configuration and a short cost estimate so procurement can budget.

I am OK to schedule the tech sync Thursday morning — send time options and I'll confirm.

Best,
Alicia
